# Vendored UI fonts

The map editor's interface face, and the monospaced face its code views use.
Both are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (the licence texts are beside
them), which allows bundling and embedding.

| File | Family | Version | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Inter-Regular.ttf`, `Inter-Medium.ttf`, `Inter-SemiBold.ttf` | Inter | 4.1 | https://github.com/rsms/inter/releases/tag/v4.1 (`extras/ttf/`) |
| `JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf` | JetBrains Mono | 2.304 | https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono/releases/tag/v2.304 (`fonts/ttf/`) |
| `ToriRSIcons.ttf` | Lucide icons (58 of them) | lucide-static 1.70.0 | https://www.npmjs.com/package/lucide-static (`font/lucide.ttf`), ISC licence: `Lucide-LICENSE.txt` |

`ToriRSIcons.ttf` is made by `tools/chrome_ui_icons_vendor.py`: the icons the
editor uses, each moved to a printable ASCII code (the chrome draws text as
bytes), under a family name of its own because it is a modified version.
`src/ui/torirs_chrome_icons.h` (generated by the same run) names each code.

These are SUBSETS, not the upstream files: Basic Latin, Latin-1 and the
dashes, quotes, arrows and marks the editor's labels use, with hinting
programs and OpenType layout tables dropped (the client rasterises with
stb_truetype, which reads neither). `tools/chrome_ui_fonts_vendor.py` makes
them from the two release archives; it needs `fonttools==4.59.2`.

A subset is a Modified Version in the OFL's terms. Neither copyright
statement declares a Reserved Font Name (checked 2026-11-09: the term appears
only in the licence's own definitions), so the subsets keep their family
names; the licence still requires that each licence text travels with the
faces, which is why both sit in this directory.
